turns.question: i am an employee of a board of park commissioners, how is my pension calculated?
turns.answer:
Your record places you in Article 12. Under the current Article 12 formula, a retirement annuity is generally:

- **2.40% of your highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years within your last 10 years of service**
- multiplied by your years of service, with a prorated amount for part of a year
- subject to an **80% maximum** of that salary average. [40 ILCS 5/12-133]

Because you are age 56, retiring before age 60 would generally reduce the annuity by **0.25% for each month or fraction of a month** that your age is below 60. That reduction does not apply to an employee retiring at age 50 or over with at least 30 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/12-133]

You currently have **21.5 years of service**, but the exact pension figure cannot be worked out without your age at withdrawal and your highest average annual salary for 4 consecutive years within your last 10 years. The Code defines salary using the applicable pay basis, such as annual, monthly, weekly, daily, or hourly pay. [40 ILCS 5/12-122]

Section 12-130 provides eligibility for retirement before age 60 after at least 10 years of service. Section 12-131 describes an accumulation-based calculation for retirement at age 60 or over. The material available here does not establish whether that calculation applies in your circumstances or provide enough information to calculate it.

The early-retirement incentive provisions are limited to specified historical eligibility windows and election deadlines, so they do not establish a general current early-retirement option. [40 ILCS 5/12-133.3; 40 ILCS 5/12-133.4; 40 ILCS 5/12-133.5]

After retirement, Article 12 provides a 3% annual increase in your basic retirement annuity, subject to the timing rules in that section. [40 ILCS 5/12-133.1]

turns.question: What does Section 11-134 say about the annuity formula?
turns.answer:
Section 11-134 provides several annuity formulas.

For an employee with at least 20 years of service who withdraws on or after January 1, 2002, one formula is **2.40% of the highest average annual salary for each year of service**. The salary basis is the highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years of service. The annuity may begin at age 55, or at age 50 with at least 30 years of service, and is reduced by **0.25% for each month or fractional month** that commencement is before age 60. Certain employees with at least 25 or 30 years of service are exempt from that reduction. The maximum is **80%** of the highest average annual salary. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

The section also gives an alternative election for an employee with at least 10 years of service. That annuity begins no earlier than age 60 and uses the same **2.40% for each year of service** formula, subject to an **80%** maximum. The highest average salary is the highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years in the last 10 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

Your 21.5 years of service are counted under the minimum-annuity service rules. Section 11-216 says that service during 6 or more months in a year counts as a year, while service of less than 6 months and at least 1 month counts as a half year. Section 11-215 identifies which work, leave, and disability periods may count as service. [40 ILCS 5/11-216] [40 ILCS 5/11-215]

The Code text available here does not provide your salary history or withdrawal date, so it is not enough to determine which election produces the larger annuity or to calculate an amount. It also does not establish any conclusion under Sections 11-221 or 11-164, which Section 11-215 references.

turns.question: What does Article 22A of the Pension Code provide?
turns.answer:
Article 22A concerns the **Illinois State Board of Investment** and the investment of public retirement-system assets.

The Code provisions reviewed describe these main functions:

- Retirement boards may invest in commingled investment funds established and maintained by the Illinois State Board of Investment under Article 22A. [40 ILCS 5/15-167.1]
- A retirement board may transfer all of its investments to that Board for management and administration. After the transfer, the retirement board’s authority to make investments ends, and investments are made under Article 22A. [40 ILCS 5/16-179.1]
- The State Employees Deferred Compensation Plan is developed and administered by the Illinois State Board of Investment. [40 ILCS 5/24-104]
- Fiduciaries must act solely for participants and beneficiaries, provide benefits and pay reasonable administrative expenses, use prudent care, diversify investments unless clearly imprudent, and follow the governing Article. [40 ILCS 5/1-109]

Article 22A therefore deals with **investment management and fiduciary administration**, not your retirement age, service credit, or pension amount. Your record places you in Article 11, but the provisions reviewed here do not determine your Article 11 pension benefit.
